points.description: Defines ESN as a type of Recurrent Neural Network with at least one cyclic/feedback connection (recurrent connections), and says that only the output layer weights are trained/updated.
points.partial_credit: Half if only one of the two ideas (recurrent with feedback connections, or only output weights trained) is given, or the definition is vague.

points.description: Explains the difference from FF NNs: ESN has feedback (cyclic) connections while a FF NN does not, so an ESN can approximate dynamic systems while a FF NN cannot.
points.partial_credit: Half if only the feedback vs no-feedback contrast or only the dynamic-systems point is given, or the contrast is vague.

rubric.notes: Full marks: P1 needs ESN named as a recurrent network with feedback/cyclic connections plus the output-only training; P2 needs the contrast with FF NNs (feedback vs none, and dynamic systems). Half marks for a point that is vague or has only one of its two ideas. Zero for a point that is wrong, e.g. calling an ESN feedforward or saying all weights are trained.
